reader.requirement: At 85 the compiler must accept FUNCTION MIN with a parenthesized list of one or more arguments (numeric, alphabetic or alphanumeric; literals, identifiers, expressions; table ALL subscripts), yield an alphanumeric result usable as an identifier (and reference-modifiable) or a numeric/integer result only in an arithmetic expression, and refuse a missing or empty list.

edition-consulted.switches: catalog IntroducedIn 85 against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel (COBOL1502/COBOL1503 window); the function is defined at 85
construct function-empty-argument-list-2002: an empty '( )' is COBOL0900 at 85 (braces of §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.2 require an argument); at 2023 it parses and the arity check refuses it (COBOL1504)

construct numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (DISPLAY, MOVE, ADD operand) is COBOL0900 at 85 per §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4; legal at 2023

construct repository-function-2002: at 85 the keyword-omitted form never routes to the intrinsic, so NAME (args) is an ordinary (undefined) data reference, COBOL1639; at 2023 it is COBOL1543 unless the REPOSITORY declares it

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicCatalog.cs, VersionConformancePass.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior; TryBindAllArgument, BindIntrinsicArgs and the arity check read no edition; the CobolIntrinsics runtime bodies take no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an empty '( )' is refused as an edition construct (COBOL0900) and a numeric/integer result written where an identifier stands is refused (SR4); at 2023 the empty list reaches the arity check and the identifier placement is legal; the format's own argument count and ALL handling is the same code at both

reader.notes: MIN's catalog row is Variadic 1..inf, 'p', result FollowsUniformArguments, so the alphanumeric form is an identifier (MOVE, DISPLAY, ref-mod legal at 85) while the numeric form trips SR4's edition gate outside an arithmetic expression, as §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR3/SR4 require. Format clause cite is the description (format text too short for cite.py).

refuter.evidence: MIN (3; 1; 2)=1; MIN (1 - 2)=-1 (one expression) vs MIN (1 -2)=-2 (two arguments); MIN (- 3 + 1 5)=-2; DPC MIN (7; 1,25)=1,25; data named MIN/MOD/MIDRANGE as arguments MIN=4; PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE reversed alphabet MIN ("A" "Z")=Z (simple-condition comparison); MIN (X3 N3) mixed alphanumeric/numeric refused COBOL1627; numeric MIN (1 2) (1:1) refused COBOL1629 (SR2: only alphanumeric MIN may be ref-modified); 18-digit MIN (BIG NBIG)=-999999999999999999. probes under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-176/runs (acc2-001, dpc-001, ref2-001, ref3-001, ref4-001, pcs-001, big-002, kw-002, lc-001), all --std 85 via run_probe.py. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR2 (comma and semicolon followed by a space are separators anywhere a space is); OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1 (argument is identifier, literal or arithmetic expression); OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2 (ref-mod only for alphanumeric functions); OK §1989:A.2.2 (ALL subscripts, rightmost ALL varies fastest). Class e does not apply (no file I/O in the format). No program the format refuses compiled, none it admits was refused, every value matched the 1985 returned-value rules. Side note, not this rule: diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses (cosmetic).
